open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list configuration re-read
open_points.text: “the checks and the read use that one opened file” conflicts with A16 rule 2: “the kernel reads the configuration file and compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ ... it re-reads it”
open_points.question: When checking for a changed token list, must hashing, security checks and parsing use one opened descriptor and one byte snapshot, or does “re-ads” require a second secure open whose bytes may differ?
options: Use one securely opened descriptor and parse the same bytes that were hashed
Securely open once to detect a change, then securely open again to parse
Reuse the descriptor but seek and read the file a second time
open_points.default_guess: Use one securely opened descriptor and parse the same bytes that were hashed

open_points.subject: installation path traversal for an empty component sequence
open_points.text: “an empty one, from a repeated or trailing `/`, skipped” and “the last component for reading” do not say what happens when no non-empty component exists
open_points.question: What does load_installation do when its path is empty or consists only of slashes, leaving no last component to open for reading?
options: Refuse because there is no file component
Treat the working-directory or root anchor as the candidate and then refuse it as non-regular
Reject the path earlier as an invalid configuration-file path
open_points.default_guess: Refuse because there is no file component

open_points.subject: release host prerequisites for secure path walking
open_points.text: “each directory on the way opened with `O_PATH` and `O_DIRECTORY`” but A20 declares only “a Linux without `O_NOFOLLOW`” unsupported and names no Linux version
open_points.question: Is a Linux host lacking `O_PATH` or `O_DIRECTORY` unsupported like one lacking `O_NOFOLLOW`, or must the kernel detect that condition and refuse startup in a defined way?
options: Declare Linux without any required flag unsupported and perform no test
Test all required flags or facilities at startup and refuse with a defined start error
Specify a minimum Linux version that supplies every required facility
open_points.default_guess: Declare Linux without any required flag unsupported and perform no test
